title: A projective pure spreadout after a finite quotient of a local base
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a commutative local ring, meaning that $\mathfrak m$ is its unique maximal ideal. Let $R\to B$ be a finitely presented homomorphism of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], let $\Sigma\subseteq B$ contain $1$ and be closed under multiplication, and let $N$ be a finitely presented $\Sigma^{-1}B$-module. Here localization consists of fractions with denominators in the indicated multiplicative subset, and finitely presented means the cokernel of a map between finite rank free modules. There exist a finitely generated ideal $I\subseteq\mathfrak m$, an element $s\in\Sigma$, and a finitely presented module $P$ over $D=(B/IB)[1/\bar s]$, with the following properties. The module $P$ is projective over $R/I$ [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. If $\bar\Sigma$ denotes the image of $\Sigma$ in $D$, there is a $\bar\Sigma^{-1}D$-linear isomorphism $\theta:\bar\Sigma^{-1}P\xrightarrow{\sim}N/IN$. The map $j:P\to N/IN$, $p\mapsto\theta(p/1)$, is universally injective over $R/I$: for every $R/I$-module $T$, the map $j\otimes1_T:P\otimes_{R/I}T\to(N/IN)\otimes_{R/I}T$ is injective [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. No flatness assumption on $N$ over $R$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0AT8, lemma-find-pure-spreadout, equation-star and its definition of pure spreadout; principal-open spreadout B_s constructed in the proof

proof.text: Choose a finite presentation $N=\operatorname{coker}(H:(\Sigma^{-1}B)^a\to(\Sigma^{-1}B)^b)$. A product $d\in\Sigma$ of its finitely many entry denominators gives a matrix $H_0$ over $B$ whose localization is $dH$. Put $M=\operatorname{coker}(H_0:B^a\to B^b)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact] and the fraction/tensor identification [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-over-base] (with base and algebra both $B$ and module $B$), localizing this presentation gives the cokernel of $dH$. Since $d$ is a unit, its image equals that of $H$, giving a specified isomorphism $\Sigma^{-1}M\cong N$. For an empty matrix take $d=1$.

Put $k=R/\mathfrak m$, $\overline B=B/\mathfrak mB$ and $\overline M=M/\mathfrak mM$. The finite algebra generators of $B$ also generate $\overline B$ over the field $k$. A field is Noetherian (its ideals are $0$ and the whole field), so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] makes $\overline B$ Noetherian. The images of the $b$ presentation generators generate $\overline M$. The quotient identification $X\otimes_R k\cong X/\mathfrak mX$, $x\otimes\bar r\mapsto rx$, and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-over-base] identify $N/\mathfrak mN$ with $\overline\Sigma^{-1}\overline M$. Hence $K=\ker(\overline M\to\overline\Sigma^{-1}\overline M)$ is finitely generated by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite].

Choose generators $x_1,\ldots,x_t$ of $K$. For each $i$, the fraction criterion $x_i/1=0$ gives $s_i\in\Sigma$ with $s_ix_i=0$. Put $s=\prod_i s_i$ (take $s=1$ when $K=0$). Then $sK=0$. Set $C=B_s$ and $L=M_s$. The ring $C$ is finitely presented over $R$: append one variable $z$ and the single relation $sz-1$ to a finite presentation of $B$, using a polynomial representative of $s$. By [lem-trf-localization-preserves-finite-presentation], $L$ is finitely presented over $C$. By the tensor/localization formula [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-over-base], $L/\mathfrak mL=(\overline M)_s$. The map $(\overline M)_s\to\overline\Sigma^{-1}\overline M$ is injective: if $x/s^e$ maps to zero then $x\in K$, hence $sx=0$, so $x/s^e=0$. Consequently multiplication by every $t\in\Sigma$ on $L/\mathfrak mL$ is injective, since its action on $N/\mathfrak mN$ is invertible.

Apply [lem-sfb-local-algebra-module-noetherian-subring-model] to $C,L$ over $R$. Write $R_0,C_0,L_0,\mathfrak n$ for its data. Put $I=\mathfrak nR$, $A=R/I$ and $k_0=R_0/\mathfrak n$. Since $\mathfrak n$ is finitely generated and contained in $\mathfrak m$, so is $I$. The inclusion $R_0\to R$ induces $k_0\to A$. Put $D=C/IC=(B/IB)[1/\bar s]$ and $P=L/IL$. By [lem-pc-fp-module-base-change] applied to $C\to D$, $P$ is finitely presented over $D$; the identification $D\otimes_C L\cong L/IL$ sends $\bar c\otimes l$ to $cl$. The model isomorphism gives
$$P\cong A\otimes_{k_0}(L_0/\mathfrak nL_0).$$
Explicitly the quotient of $R\otimes_{R_0}L_0$ sends $\bar r\otimes\bar l$ to $[r\otimes l]$; its inverse sends $[r\otimes l]$ to $\bar r\otimes\bar l$. Both respect the balanced relations because $\mathfrak nA=0$.

The module $V=L_0/\mathfrak nL_0$ is a vector space over the field $k_0$, hence projective by [lem-weil-pbc-vector-space-projective]. Apply [lem-trf-local-projective-tensor-base-change] to $k_0\to A$. The displayed isomorphism shows that $P$ is projective over $A$, and [lem-weil-pbc-projective-module-flat] makes it flat over $A$. No finite rank over $A$ is asserted or required. The ring $A$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m/I$: ideals maximal in $A$ correspond to maximal ideals of $R$ containing $I$, so there is exactly this one.

For each $t\in\Sigma$, multiplication $t:P\to P$ is an $A$-linear map with projective source and flat target. Its reduction modulo $\mathfrak m/I$ is multiplication by $t$ on $L/\mathfrak mL$, injective by step 3. Thus [lem-trf-local-universal-injective-residue] applies and shows that $t\otimes1_T$ is injective on $P\otimes_A T$ for every $A$-module $T$. Let $\overline\Sigma$ denote the image in $D$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-over-base], the map $P\otimes_A T\to\overline\Sigma^{-1}P\otimes_A T$ is localization at $\overline\Sigma$. An element in its kernel is killed by some image of $t\in\Sigma$ by the fraction zero criterion; the injectivity just proved forces that element to be zero. This proves universal injectivity of $P\to\overline\Sigma^{-1}P$ directly, without an uncited colimit argument.

Finally [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-over-base] identifies
$$\overline\Sigma^{-1}P=\overline\Sigma^{-1}(L/IL)\cong(\Sigma^{-1}L)/I(\Sigma^{-1}L)\cong N/IN.$$
Here quotient and localization commute by the same tensor formula with $R\to C$ and the $R$-module $R/I$; the quotient map is $x\otimes\bar r\mapsto rx\bmod I$. The last isomorphism comes from step 1, since inverting $s\in\Sigma$ first does not change localization at $\Sigma$. On fractions these maps send $[l]/t$ to $[l/t]$, so their composite $\theta$ is linear over $\overline\Sigma^{-1}D$ and the composite $P\to N/IN$ is precisely $p\mapsto\theta(p/1)$. Tensoring an isomorphism preserves injectivity, so step 6 gives the required universal injectivity of this specified $j$.

The 7 steps follow 0AT8 and are correct: denominators are cleared with a common d∈Σ; the closed-fibre kernel is finitely generated because B/mB is Noetherian; the kernel is killed by s=∏s_i, so B_s, M_s are finitely presented and every t∈Σ is injective on L/mL; the new model is applied with I=nR; P≅(R/I)⊗_{k0}(L0/nL0) is projective and flat over the local ring R/I; 05FQ makes multiplication by t universally injective, and a fraction argument gives universal injectivity of P→Σ̄⁻¹P; finally θ: Σ̄⁻¹P≅N/IN. I checked N=0, 0∈Σ, R a field, K=0 and infinite-dimensional fibres. The new node is true: take A' generated by the coefficients over Z and R0=A'_{A'∩m}, which embeds in R because elements outside the contraction are units of R. It is strictly smaller than the item (no quotient, projectivity or injectivity clause) and is not a duplicate: the trf/pbc coefficient-model and Noetherian-tower nodes are algebra-only, unlocalized, or tower comparisons. lean.statement: theorem exists_projective_pureSpreadout_of_finitePresentation {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] {B : Type v} [CommRing B] [Algebra R B] [Algebra.FinitePresentation R B] (S : Submonoid B) (N : Type w) [AddCommGroup N] [Module (Localization S) N] [Module B N] [IsScalarTower B (Localization S) N] [Module R N] [IsScalarTower R B N] [Module.FinitePresentation (Localization S) N] : ∃ I : Ideal R, I.FG ∧ I ≤ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R ∧ ∃ s : S, ∃ (P : Type (max u v w)) (_ : AddCommGroup P) (_ : Module (Localization.Away (Ideal.Quotient.mk (I.map (algebraMap R B)) s)) P) (_ : Module B P) (_ : IsScalarTower B (Localization.Away (Ideal.Quotient.mk (I.map (algebraMap R B)) s)) P) (_ : Module (R ⧸ I) P) (_ : Module B (N ⧸ (I • ⊤ : Submodule R N))), (∀ (r : R) (p : P), Ideal.Quotient.mk I r • p = algebraMap R (Localization.Away (Ideal.Quotient.mk (I.map (algebraMap R B)) s)) r • p) ∧ (∀ (b : B) (n : N), b • (Submodule.Quotient.mk n : N ⧸ (I • ⊤ : Submodule R N)) = Submodule.Quotient.mk (b • n)) ∧ Module.FinitePresentation (Localization.Away (Ideal.Quotient.mk (I.map (algebraMap R B)) s)) P ∧ Module.Projective (R ⧸ I) P ∧ ∃ (j : P →ₗ[B] (N ⧸ (I • ⊤ : Submodule R N))) (jA : P →ₗ[R ⧸ I] (N ⧸ (I • ⊤ : Submodule R N))), (∀ p : P, jA p = j p) ∧ IsLocalizedModule S j ∧ ∀ (T : Type (max u v w z)) [AddCommGroup T] [Module (R ⧸ I) T], Function.Injective (jA.rTensor T)
